name: LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM0L130x datasheet SLASEX0D (features); LaunchPad user guide SLAU869E (board parts, jumpers J16 and J17, Figure 2-9 header pinout); measured on the board 2026-10-06 (mspm0l1306/README.md)

columns.head: The chip: MSPM0L1306
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 32 million steps a second (32 MHz)
Flash: 64 kB
Holds the program. Kept when the power is off
RAM: 4 kB
Working memory while it runs. This is what runs out first
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.62 to 3.6 V, so 5 V parts need care

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: 28 pins
Plain on/off pins: LEDs, buttons, control lines. 26 reach the board's headers
UART: 2
Simple serial text, one wire each way: GPS, the computer's terminal
I2C: 2 / SPI: 1
Shared two-wire bus for sensors / fast bus for displays and memory chips
ADC: 1
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps (12-bit). No general-purpose DAC to make one
Op-amps: 2, comparator: 1
Amplify small signals, like the light sensor's
Timers: 4
Timing and PWM for dimming LEDs

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
USB debug probe, red LED, color LED, 2 buttons plus reset, light sensor, thermistor
Headers
40 pins in four rows (J1 to J4); 8 of the positions are not connected
Not on the chip
No radio, no AES or random-number hardware, no math accelerator, no general-purpose DAC
Watch out
Only 4 kB of RAM: stacks and buffers have to be sized by hand
